core_principles.name: Receptive Architecture
core_principles.description: Listen to the code and let patterns emerge naturally rather than forcing premature abstractions
core_principles.practical_application: I prefer to start with concrete implementations and extract abstractions only when clear patterns become apparent. This approach has served me well in building scalable systems at System73 and implementing AI solutions at XalDigital.
core_principles.example: When building the P2P streaming platform, I initially implemented specific video handling logic before extracting generic media processing patterns, which led to a more intuitive and maintainable architecture.

core_principles.name: Experimental Iteration
core_principles.description: Build multiple approaches to explore the solution space, with each component doing one thing exceptionally well
core_principles.practical_application: I regularly create spike solutions and prototypes to understand problems deeply before committing to implementation approaches. This reduces technical debt and leads to better architectural decisions.
core_principles.example: For the computer vision quality control system, I built three different model architectures before selecting the optimal approach, which saved weeks of refactoring later.

core_principles.name: Essential Simplicity
core_principles.description: Remove everything that doesn't serve the core purpose, making code read like well-written prose
core_principles.practical_application: I prioritize readable, self-documenting code over clever solutions. Every abstraction must earn its existence by providing clear value.
core_principles.example: In the weather MCP server, I chose clear, descriptive function names and simple data structures over complex inheritance hierarchies, making the codebase approachable for new contributors.

core_principles.name: Collaborative Decoupling
core_principles.description: Design for others by minimizing coupling and creating clear, stable interfaces
core_principles.practical_application: I apply dependency inversion consistently and design APIs that welcome contribution and modification. Code should be ego-free and focused on the best solution.
core_principles.example: The trade promotion MCP server uses well-defined interfaces that allow easy extension of new trading strategies without modifying core business logic.

technical_opinions.on_ai_ml: AI/ML should solve real problems, not just demonstrate technical capability. The most valuable AI applications are those that augment human decision-making rather than trying to replace human judgment entirely.
technical_opinions.on_distributed_systems: Complexity should be introduced only when it's justified by actual requirements. Start simple and evolve architecture as the system and team grow.
technical_opinions.on_team_scaling: Technical practices and culture are more important than individual talent. A team with good practices will consistently outperform a team of brilliant individuals without good processes.
technical_opinions.on_technology_choice: Choose technologies based on team expertise, problem requirements, and long-term maintainability rather than novelty or personal preference.
